title: Adversarial Suffix Robustness Across Safety Benchmarks

original_idea.title: Adversarial Suffix Robustness Across Safety Benchmarks
original_idea.problem: Adversarial suffixes appended to prompts can bypass safety training. It is unknown whether models with high safety benchmark scores are more robust to adversarial suffixes than lower-scoring models.
original_idea.direction: Use publicly available adversarial suffix generation methods (e.g., GCG attack simplified or pre-computed suffixes from published papers). Append these to 30-40 safety benchmark items from AILuminate. Evaluate 2-3 open-source models. Measure whether standard benchmark safety score predicts adversarial suffix robustness. Report a correlation coefficient and discuss implications.
original_idea.why_it_matters: If high benchmark scores do not predict adversarial robustness, then safety benchmarks are not measuring relevant safety properties. This would motivate including adversarial robustness in standard evaluation protocols.
original_idea.relevant_context: GCG adversarial suffix attacks (Zou et al. 2023) are well-known. JailbreakBench and HarmBench include adversarial attack results. AILuminate does not include adversarial suffix conditions.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: testing whether benchmark scores predict adversarial robustness is a fundamental validity question for the safety evaluation field.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Advanced: GCG attack implementation and adversarial suffix generation require significant ML and optimization knowledge beyond beginner CS student level.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable: correlation analysis between benchmark scores and suffix robustness on 30-40 items across 2-3 models.

novelty.reasoning: The relationship between standard safety benchmarks and adversarial suffix robustness is an active research area. JailbreakBench (NeurIPS 2024) provides an open robustness benchmark. 'Bag of Tricks' (NeurIPS 2024) benchmarks jailbreak attacks on LLMs. AmpleGCG demonstrates universal transferable adversarial suffix generation. Research on token position in GCG attacks (2025) highlights blind spots in safety evaluations. The specific correlation analysis between standard benchmark scores and GCG robustness is a valid contribution, but the broader question is partially addressed by JailbreakBench and HarmBench.
